programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Bha stoirm mhòr san Achadh Fhiadhaich ’s a nis tha bùrach mòr ann. Tha glanadh mòr ri dhèanamh. Following a huge storm in Wild Meadow, there is now a big mess and a lot of clearing up to be done.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Baba a' sealltainn g' eil e fàs a cheart cho comasach ri càch nuair a chuidicheas e faoileag bheag a chaidh a glacadh am measg sreang iasgach air an tràigh. Baba helps rescue a baby seagull caught up in fishing twine on the beach, proving that he is now as capable as his older sister and friends.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha fleadh gu bhith aig sgioba nan luch 's tha Mossy trang a cruinneachadh dhearcagan air a shon. Ged a tha Oona 's Baba ga chuideachadh, tha cùisean a' dol bun os cionn orra, gun aca ach aon dhearcag aig deireadh an là! Mossy is busy collecting berries for the feast the shrew crew are planning. Oona and Baba decide to help their friend, but disaster strikes and they are left with nothing but a single berry at the end of the day.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Chan eil sgeul air Fuigheag an-duigh is tha Boban bochd a’ feuchainn ri lorg. Càite fon ghrèin a bheil e? There’s no sign of Fuigheag today and poor Boban is searching for him. Where on earth is he?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha na Losgannan a’ campachadh a-muigh le teant, geansaidhean agus marsmalothan. On a chilly day, the Froglets enjoy camping outside with a tent, sweaters and marshmallows.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Mairead Màiri agus Aneirin còmhla rithe agus iad ag ullachadh mìlseag rus le raosaran-dubha. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil an stuth a tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach ciamar a thathar a’ dèanamh sùgh raosar-dubh. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ mhìlseag rus ullachadh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe. Linda is joined by Margaret Mary and Aneirin to make blackcurrant rice pudding. Before they start cooking they have to ensure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about how blackcurrant juice is made and then return to the kitchen to make the rice pudding, before sitting down to tuck in.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Catriona Mhoireach a’ leughadh An Solas air an Oidhche. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh ’s a dhealbhachadh le Marie Voight agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Catriona Murray reads An Solas air an Oidhche, written and illustrated by Marie Voight and translated into Gaelic by Donald John Macleod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Chan eil Stella toilichte oir tha aice ri dhol gu taigh granaidh aig an deireadh-sheachdain ‘s chan eil i den bheachd gum bi sin ro shaorsnail. Cuideachd, tha planaichean aice le Mia is Freya. Dè nì i? Stella isn’t happy as she has to go to grandma’s house at the weekend and she doesn’t think that will be very relaxing. Also, she has plans with Mia and Freya. What will she do?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha èiginn eadar trì ginealaich an-diugh air Là nam Màthraichean ach tha e fortanach gu bheil Stella faisg air làimh airson gnothaichean a rèiteachadh. There’s distress between three generations today on Mother’s Day, but it’s fortunate that Stella is close by to reconcile matters.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Ged a tha na saor-làithean air tòiseachadh do sgoilearan Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, tha latha a bharrachd aig an luchd-teagaisg airson beagan trèanaidh. Tha an t-eòlaiche-inntinn Sìleas Stern os cionn sheiseanan gus sìth agus càirdeas a stèidheachadh am measg an luchd-obrach. Although the holidays have started for the pupils of Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, the teachers have an in-service day. Mr Mackle is keen to establish better relationships between his staff and has invited psychologist Sìleas Stern to run team building sessions that he hopes will bring peace and harmony.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha Stoirm Catatumbo a’ leudachadh gu luath is tha an suidheachadh a’ fàs air leth cunnartach – ach dè tha ga adhbharachadh? Feumaidh Na Neachdan seo a rannsachadh airson faighinn a-mach dè a th’ air a chùlaibh! The Catatumbo Storm is expanding rapidly and the situation is getting very dangerous, but what has caused it? The Neachdan must investigate to find out what is behind it.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek 'Pluto' Murray hosts a fun knockout amateur DIY competition where couples go head to head. Derek 'Pluto' Moireach le farpais spòrsail DIY is cupail a’ strì an aghaidh a chèile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Coinnichidh sinn ris an neach-ionnsachaidh Cailean Scott MacCoinnich à Eilean Leòdhais agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ lorg seann tobar slànachaidh air an Eilean Dubh. Joy Dunlop continues to guide us through the first steps to speak Gaelic. We meet Gaelic learner Colin Scott Mackenzie who lives on the Isle of Lewis, and a poorly Calum Maclean tries out the healing properties of an ancient clootie well on the Black Isle. Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay MacMahon walks along the beaches of Barra with Michael Buchanan. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ coiseachd air tràighean Bharraigh le Mìcheal Bochanan.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Gilleasbuig Macdonald investigates complaints about the behaviour of campervan users in Skye. Tha Gilleasbuig MacDhòmhnaill a’ rannsachadh gearainnean mu dhol-a-mach luchd bhanaichean campachaidh san Eilean Sgitheanach.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha Evelyn Coull NicLeòid a’ gabhail cuairt chun nan Eileanan a Deas, gu Uibhist, Barraigh agus Bhatarsaigh gus coinneachadh ri daoine, cuid aig a bheil ceanglaichean làidir agus cuid eile a bha a’ fuireach ann am bailtean a tha a-nis air fhalamhachadh. Evelyn Coull MacLeod takes a journey to the Southern Isles - to Uist, Barra and Vatersay, where she meets people who have strong connections to or have lived in villages that are now abandoned.

programme.title: Patagonia
programme.desc: Keith's journey takes him deep into Argentine Patagonia, where he kayaks to the awe-inspiring Perito Moreno Glacier.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Am buannaiche dhuaisean Hannah Rarity agus còmhlan-ciùil, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Anns an t-seata, The Leaving agus Christmas Came Early. Award-winning singer Hannah Rarity and band, recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen. The set includes The Leaving and Christmas Came Early.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Angela clashes with angry locals shouting about short-term lets. Betty and Dido de-escalate things and share some home truths. There’s a sticky situation when an activist called Adam sneaks through the catflap with a tube of superglue. Meanwhile, Daniel tests Katie’s management methods by renegotiating his contract. And a corporate relaunch that is definitely not a party features costumes, cocktails, new clients and wild dance moves. Ultimately the rivals seem to be getting closer than ever.

programme.title: This World

programme.title: How to Build a Cathedral
programme.desc: The great cathedrals were the wonders of the medieval world - the tallest buildings since the pyramids and the showpieces of medieval Christianity. Yet they were built at a time when most of us lived in hovels. Architectural historian Jon Cannon explores who the people were that built them and how they were able to achieve such a bold vision.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. In the second of the quarter-finals, three postgraduate students from Brasenose College, Oxford, pit their wits against a trio of Douglas Adams fans who call themselves the Hitchhikers, in honour of the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. They compete to draw together the connections between elements which, at first glance, seem utterly random: P J Tracy, Nicci French, Ellery Queen and Grant Naylor.

programme.title: Hockney
programme.desc: Documentary about artist David Hockney, from his early life in working-class Bradford to his relocation to Hollywood, with access to his personal archive of photographs and film.

programme.title: The Interview
programme.desc: David Hockney was one of the world's most successful and influential artists of our time. At 11, he wanted to be an artist. At 87, he was still creating new works - happiest when making 'joyful' art and always innovating with his iPad. His art has sold for millions. In a film originally broadcast in April 2025, ahead of his biggest show ever opening in Paris, the Bradford-born star talks to Katie Razzall about growing old, a recent visit from the King and his two big loves - smoking and painting.

programme.title: Hockney: Double Portrait
programme.desc: An intimate documentary profile of artist David Hockney as he returns to the theme of double portraits, three decades after some of his most iconic works, like Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy. From 2003.

programme.title: Face to Face
programme.desc: In an interview first broadcast in 1996, artist David Hockney talks to Jeremy Isaacs about painting, designing for the opera and his growing deafness.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes considers America during the 1920s and 30s, including the skyscraper as the image of modernism, the Depression, regionalist art and black art.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross uncorks an episode of the show fizzing with fun and excitement at the South of England Showground in West Sussex. Among the stalls at the Ardingly Antiques Fair, he quizzes punters about a mystery metal object. While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross uncorks an episode of the show fizzing with fun and excitement at the South of England Showground in West Sussex. Among the stalls at the Ardingly Antiques Fair, he quizzes punters about a mystery metal object. While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross uncorks an episode of the show fizzing with fun and excitement at the South of England Showground in West Sussex. Among the stalls at the Ardingly Antiques Fair, he quizzes punters about a mystery metal object. While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. This week they are looking at our fantastic fruit, making an apple and bramble crumble with a Drambuie custard. Joining them in the kitchen are Aberdeenshire soft fruit famer Ross Mitchell and food and drink writer Rosalind Erskine, who has selected a Scottish rum flavoured with rhubarb.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: Fishing and horse riding are staple pastimes in the Borders, along the River Tweed horses are ingrained in people's lives as much as the clear water running through the river and this is certainly the case for trainer Katie Scott. This episode sees Katie prepare horses for Kelso races in horrific rainy and sleety conditions, but she battles through it and manages to get three horses to the races. On the river, ghillie Colin Bell has some returning fishing clients seeking the best pools on the Upper Floors fishing beat. Colin has high expectations and uses traditional 'hand lining' skills to get his clients a majestic Tweed salmon. In Kelso, Tweedside Tackle are moving their fishing tackle shop across the road and will need to move over 20,000 hooks, reels, rods and waders. And in Peebles, as the Tweedlove festival gets under way, organisers Neil and Fiona Dalgleish make sure all the valleys' biking fanatics head off in style.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: For thousands of years prized salmon stocks have faced a varying degree of threats to their existence. In this episode, Eddie Weatherly and his river bailiff team respond to more calls that salmon poachers are active along the river, the search is on and, under the cover of darkness, the team lie in wait to see if the poachers turn up. In Kelso, it's one of the busiest weekends of the year for the Ednam House hotel. Manager Margaret Livingstone-Evans has three weddings across three days, a bridal conundrum! In Peebles, Ruth Hinks has 5,000 chocolate brownies to make for a charity campaign, but little does she know that husband David has a special surprise lined up to reward her for all her hard work. On Cowbog Farm, farmer Robert Wilson, daughter Lottie and father Ron are testing the cattle for TB and far more importantly for daughter Lottie, they're checking to see if her favourite cow is pregnant. And at Floors Stud, it's a big day for all involved as Tattersalls auctioneer Todd Watt visits to decide just how many potential million-pound horses will go in the biggest of horse sales.

programme.title: The Agency: Unfiltered
programme.desc: The academy competitors are creating a piece of content that will be a collaboration between two pairs. Simmie and Tasha are making a piece of content about traumas they have both experienced while travelling, and Debs and Nasti are making a piece of content about Debs' favourite cheat meal.

programme.title: The Agency: Unfiltered
programme.desc: Nicole decides whether to stay signed to the agency, Darby tells her story on Charlotte Dawson’s podcast, and Kirsten and Amy announce the winner of this year’s academy.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Callum’s web of lies unravels to a stunned and devastated Kelly-Marie, and Mikey is left torn when he is given the chance to tell his side of the story. Meanwhile, Angus worries he pushed Amber into therapy before she is ready, and Drew finds himself the victim of extortion.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Beth is ill and has taken to her bed. Ian and Gordon have popped over to give Eric a hand. If ever there’s a time Beth is desperate to be left alone, it’s now - but on hearing about Beth’s flu, Christine turns up with homemade soup. The interruptions continue as Cathy and Colin arrive, who suggest all Beth needs is someone with a bit of personality to go and see her. Up and down the stairs like a yo-yo, Eric tends to Beth’s needs, reassuring her that nobody will disturb her. But the neighbours have decided Eric isn’t coping, and it’s a competition to see whether a hot toddy or soup made from a good ham bone will do the trick in nursing Beth back to health.

programme.title: The Chief
programme.desc: The Chief is made aware of a potential newspaper scoop featuring a leaked recording that could sink his whole career. His paranoia soon becomes all-consuming, and he suspects those around him in the force - even his own family - of betrayal. These explosive revelations threaten to eclipse his revolutionary new police work policy, where he redefines the very nature of crime. As his relationship with government, press and the public deteriorates, will he be forced to redefine the very nature of the Chief?

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: Janey and Ashley don hard hats and head for a construction site. They are set to work making mortar, and they find out just how hard it is to build a simple wall. Next up, they have to get their heads around more complicated tools to connect cold and hot water pipes. Their work is then put to the test when it’s hooked up to the live water main, and it could be a disaster if the site starts filling up with water! However, their biggest challenge comes when they have to insulate a wall. The job involves joinery, accurate measuring and trying not to waste expensive materials. Can Ashley and Janey get past the hilarity of the word ‘dwang’? Can they put in the hard graft to see the shift through? And which one will be named ‘best employee’ and avoid that last awful job?

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Sally is in the thick of lambing on her croft in Caithness, where unseasonal weather is taking its toll. She loses three lambs in one day and has to call out the vet for a ewe that has had a difficult birth. Meanwhile, her son William comes down with chicken pox. Hot off the heels of lambing his dad’s sheep, it’s the turn of Nick’s easy-cares - but it turns out to be far from easy. Bad weather means vulnerable newborns need to be brought inside, which is not good for this breed. In Fife, Jo and Andy decide to dig up 100 acres of failed wheat, which they resow with oats. And it’s the start of showing season as they select their finest North Cheviot tups, ewes and lambs for the whole family to compete at their local show.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: The last programme of the spring series, Dougie and the team are at Ingliston for The Royal Highland Show. Cammy catches up with a professional sheep dresser as he makes finishing touches before showing his Bleu du Maines. As Landward celebrates fifty years on air, Dougie looks back on show coverage from the archive. Rosie gets a taste of Aberdeenshire in the food and drink hall showcasing artisan producers, Arlene visits the honey tent to find about the complexities of judging the amber nectar, Cammy’s hoping to win a red rosette in the show ring with his Jersey dairy cow. And Dougie steps into the main ring to follow the spectacular grand parade.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty plants meconopsis, and Brian is in the 6x8 greenhouse looking at what you can do if you have this standard-sized glasshouse. Also, a visit to a great community garden in the Easterhouse area of Glasgow that is used and enjoyed by a range of groups in the local community, and handy hints. Kirsty and Brian start a new feature that gives 'everything you need to know' plant profiles on some of the country’s most popular garden varieties - from growing patterns and soil preference to pruning plans. Throughout the series are fact files on some of the plants most often found in viewers' plots.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. This week they are looking at our fantastic fruit, making an apple and bramble crumble with a Drambuie custard. Joining them in the kitchen are Aberdeenshire soft fruit famer Ross Mitchell and food and drink writer Rosalind Erskine, who has selected a Scottish rum flavoured with rhubarb.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: Fishing and horse riding are staple pastimes in the Borders, along the River Tweed horses are ingrained in people's lives as much as the clear water running through the river and this is certainly the case for trainer Katie Scott. This episode sees Katie prepare horses for Kelso races in horrific rainy and sleety conditions, but she battles through it and manages to get three horses to the races. On the river, ghillie Colin Bell has some returning fishing clients seeking the best pools on the Upper Floors fishing beat. Colin has high expectations and uses traditional 'hand lining' skills to get his clients a majestic Tweed salmon. In Kelso, Tweedside Tackle are moving their fishing tackle shop across the road and will need to move over 20,000 hooks, reels, rods and waders. And in Peebles, as the Tweedlove festival gets under way, organisers Neil and Fiona Dalgleish make sure all the valleys' biking fanatics head off in style.

programme.title: Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star
programme.desc: The MUAs are booked to create summer party looks for global retailer H&M Beauty for an online campaign that will be seen by millions. Joining Val and Dom is guest judge and global creative director for the brand Marjorie Lacombe-Jelinek. The MUAs have just two hours to design and create party looks that focus on the brand's eyeliners, eye shadows and stand-out lip colours. Their looks and models are then screen-tested by the judges to see who has hit the brief and created the strongest look, which will then go on to be shot and featured in the global summer party campaign. This week’s creative brief is all about Seasons of Change. The MUAs are challenged to create a look inspired by a time of change in their own life. The judges want them to design bold, creative and conceptual looks in two and a half hours. Finally, the judges decide which two MUAs will go head-to-head in the Face Off elimination, a make-up skill drill under intense time pressure, after which, one MUA packs up their make-up kit and leaves the competition.

programme.title: Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star
programme.desc: The six remaining MUAs are thrown into the glossy world of fashion editorials and booked on a job for legendary music magazine Rolling Stone UK, where they must design make-up looks for Grammy-nominated DJ and producer Jayda G. Working alongside the judges are the magazine’s editor-in-chief, Cliff Joannou, and guest judge Hector Espinal, Fenty Beauty’s Global make-up artist and one of Rhianna’s personal MUAs. Each MUA is assigned a female model and mood board, and the brief for today’s feature is 90s raver. The stakes are high, as only one look will be chosen for the editorials feature/digital cover. For this week’s Creative Brief, the MUAs are challenged to produce a look that resembles a statue of how they would like to be remembered. It must include the face, head and shoulders and at least one 3D element. The two MUAs judged to have produced the weakest looks go head-to-head in the Face Off elimination, and the one who least impresses packs up their make-up kit and leaves the competition.

programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson subjects the Skoda Yeti to a remarkably thorough road test, while James May makes a rare visit to the test track in the insane Aerial Atom V8. programme.title: Football’s New Generation
programme.desc: The intimate story of England's newest recruits, charting their rise from grassroots heroes to Europe's biggest stage. Featuring Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Ollie Watkins and Marc Guehi, the documentary reveals their personal stories for the first time, with contributions from their loved ones, family and friends, as well as the veterans who mentored them to the world stage. The film charts their paths from humble beginnings, revealing for the first time the personal battles that culminated in a new breed of players representing England at Euro 2024.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve takes on four entirely new adventures to some of the remotest parts of the planet in search of precious natural wonders. In the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Steve teams up with one of the world’s best free climbers, Leo Houlding, and former Royal Marine Aldo Kane. Together, they scale the highest peak in the ancient Dedan kingdom to unearth the secrets of this 2,500-year-old civilisation. In Gabon, Steve heads deep into the jungle to find a very special group of gorillas who have learned to trust humans – but who no-one has seen for nearly a year. In Mexico, Steve travels to the Sea of Cortez – known as the world’s aquarium – on a mission to free dive with mobula rays. Although they are protected by law, this incredibly rare marine species is under threat of extinction. In Kamchatka, Steve sets out to explore the Russian tundra in autumn, when brown bears are feasting on salmon. He witnesses a pristine, untouched wilderness where wildlife is unaffected by humans – a glimpse of the world as it should be.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: From Fukushima to California, Hannah explores whether rewilding can help to heal the environmental wounds humans have inflicted on the planet.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Strictly dancer Amy Dowden turns amateur sleuth, travelling to west Wales to see if she can discover the truth behind a rumour of murder in her family history.

programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam visit Didcot to transform a garden that has been abandoned to the elements into a Bridgerton-inspired garden with a safe play area for a family's three energetic boys.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Joyce and her husband Mike spent more than 40 years living together in Guernsey. But after they both faced health challenges, they decided to return to Mike’s beloved home county of Yorkshire for a fresh start. Just months after settling in, tragedy struck when Mike passed away unexpectedly, leaving Joyce heartbroken and surrounded by a lifetime of their shared treasures. Now, with the support of close friends Brian and Adele, Joyce is ready to let go of some of the old items that have filled her new home. She hopes the auction will help her gain some space, while raising money to support her son’s work rescuing stray dogs in Thailand, honouring the couple’s shared love of animals. Auctioneer James Broad and restorer Saf Fakir roll up in West Yorkshire to lend a hand. JB uncovers pocket watches, a Victorian cauldron and a trove of jewellery, while Saf takes on three challenging restorations, including an oak coal scuttle, a writing slope and a rare pair of brass coffin stands. With a big mix of lots heading under the hammer, can JB and Saf help Joyce turn Mike’s collections into a lasting legacy and raise enough to help a cause they cared so deeply about?

programme.title: Tiger Island
programme.desc: In western Nepal, the team are continuing their tiger expedition. As monsoon storms loom and temperatures soar, the big cats are becoming more active at night. Tiger mother Goma is teaching her cubs to become independent, while Mala is struggling to keep her lone surviving cub out of trouble. The crew must adapt to the challenging conditions, deploying military-grade thermal cameras and drones to film the tigers after sunset. Under cover of darkness, the arrival of a huge dominant male presents a rare opportunity to study tiger family dynamics – but how will the male respond when he comes face to face with the cubs?

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: An exploration of the experiences of deaf people accessing healthcare across the UK, asking why communication barriers continue to affect patient care despite legal accessibility requirements. Presenter Ahmed Mudawi is joined by Lucy Warnes, chief executive of SignHealth. Together, they discuss the challenges deaf people face when accessing NHS services, the importance of the Accessible Information Standard and the ongoing campaign for equal access to healthcare.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: On 5 November 1605, a group of radical Catholic conspirators, including Guy Fawkes, came within hours of blowing up the Houses of Parliament. Their aim was to assassinate the Protestant king James I and destroy his government in an attempt to restore England to the Catholic faith. Had it not been stopped, this one moment of violence could have changed the history of the country entirely. The Gunpowder Plot was foiled, but its remembrance was written into law, and Guy Fawkes Night is still celebrated on 5 November. Lucy Worsley investigates what drove this group of men to attempt such an audacious act. She delves into the motivations and mindsets of the Catholic plotters, searching for evidence in their childhoods, the rooms where they secretly met, and where Guy Fawkes finally faced his interrogators.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are in the Lake District to fish at some of the UK’s best-loved beauty spots – Derwentwater and Watendlath Tarn. In a change from the norm, this time Bob has chosen where they go fishing in a poignant trip down memory lane for him - this was where he used to come on camping holidays with his mates, away from parents for the first time.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: On 5 November 1605, a group of radical Catholic conspirators, including Guy Fawkes, came within hours of blowing up the Houses of Parliament. Their aim was to assassinate the Protestant king James I and destroy his government in an attempt to restore England to the Catholic faith. Had it not been stopped, this one moment of violence could have changed the history of the country entirely. The Gunpowder Plot was foiled, but its remembrance was written into law, and Guy Fawkes Night is still celebrated on 5 November. Lucy Worsley investigates what drove this group of men to attempt such an audacious act. She delves into the motivations and mindsets of the Catholic plotters, searching for evidence in their childhoods, the rooms where they secretly met, and where Guy Fawkes finally faced his interrogators.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are in the Lake District to fish at some of the UK’s best-loved beauty spots – Derwentwater and Watendlath Tarn. In a change from the norm, this time Bob has chosen where they go fishing in a poignant trip down memory lane for him - this was where he used to come on camping holidays with his mates, away from parents for the first time.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve takes on four entirely new adventures to some of the remotest parts of the planet in search of precious natural wonders. In the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Steve teams up with one of the world’s best free climbers, Leo Houlding, and former Royal Marine Aldo Kane. Together, they scale the highest peak in the ancient Dedan kingdom to unearth the secrets of this 2,500-year-old civilisation. In Gabon, Steve heads deep into the jungle to find a very special group of gorillas who have learned to trust humans – but who no-one has seen for nearly a year. In Mexico, Steve travels to the Sea of Cortez – known as the world’s aquarium – on a mission to free dive with mobula rays. Although they are protected by law, this incredibly rare marine species is under threat of extinction. In Kamchatka, Steve sets out to explore the Russian tundra in autumn, when brown bears are feasting on salmon. He witnesses a pristine, untouched wilderness where wildlife is unaffected by humans – a glimpse of the world as it should be.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: From Fukushima to California, Hannah explores whether rewilding can help to heal the environmental wounds humans have inflicted on the planet.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam visit Didcot to transform a garden that has been abandoned to the elements into a Bridgerton-inspired garden with a safe play area for a family's three energetic boys.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Joyce and her husband Mike spent more than 40 years living together in Guernsey. But after they both faced health challenges, they decided to return to Mike’s beloved home county of Yorkshire for a fresh start. Just months after settling in, tragedy struck when Mike passed away unexpectedly, leaving Joyce heartbroken and surrounded by a lifetime of their shared treasures. Now, with the support of close friends Brian and Adele, Joyce is ready to let go of some of the old items that have filled her new home. She hopes the auction will help her gain some space, while raising money to support her son’s work rescuing stray dogs in Thailand, honouring the couple’s shared love of animals. Auctioneer James Broad and restorer Saf Fakir roll up in West Yorkshire to lend a hand. JB uncovers pocket watches, a Victorian cauldron and a trove of jewellery, while Saf takes on three challenging restorations, including an oak coal scuttle, a writing slope and a rare pair of brass coffin stands. With a big mix of lots heading under the hammer, can JB and Saf help Joyce turn Mike’s collections into a lasting legacy and raise enough to help a cause they cared so deeply about?

programme.title: Tiger Island
programme.desc: In western Nepal, the team are continuing their tiger expedition. As monsoon storms loom and temperatures soar, the big cats are becoming more active at night. Tiger mother Goma is teaching her cubs to become independent, while Mala is struggling to keep her lone surviving cub out of trouble. The crew must adapt to the challenging conditions, deploying military-grade thermal cameras and drones to film the tigers after sunset. Under cover of darkness, the arrival of a huge dominant male presents a rare opportunity to study tiger family dynamics – but how will the male respond when he comes face to face with the cubs?

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: An exploration of the experiences of deaf people accessing healthcare across the UK, asking why communication barriers continue to affect patient care despite legal accessibility requirements. Presenter Ahmed Mudawi is joined by Lucy Warnes, chief executive of SignHealth. Together, they discuss the challenges deaf people face when accessing NHS services, the importance of the Accessible Information Standard and the ongoing campaign for equal access to healthcare.

As the architects of this environment, can humans choose to build cities that are homes for both them and wildlife?

Glitch is determined to win Wimbledon, but he is not adhering to any of the rules, and the umpire wants him to leave. But Glitch is staying put until he can play some tennis and win the tournament, so Kyan and Xuli head on to Centre Court to take him on! Even though he is cheating, Glitch is still losing. He's had enough and finally decides to leave, but there's just one problem - he takes Centre Court with him! The Grimbots take to Grim HQ to pull Centre Court right up and out of Wimbledon. programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a hall where they watch a couple rehearsing a ballroom dance, accompanied by a piano player. He starts off playing slowly and speeds up towards the end of the dance, which gets quicker and more energetic. The Twirlywoos watch this with interest, and when the pianist steps out to take a break, they decide to investigate the piano. They start to play their own tune by running and jumping on the keys, and the dancers come in and start trying to dance to it. As the Twirlywoos get carried away, the tune gets faster and faster, and the dancers try frantically to keep up. The Hooter ends the performance by calling the Twirlywoos home, and the dancers fall in an exhausted heap on the floor! The Twirlywoos come back to the boat to find the Twirlywoo Screen. A red dot appears, and when Toodloo touches it, it makes a 'splat' sound. More dots appear, and the Twirlywoos splat them as quickly as they can. The dots appear faster and faster, and the Twirlywoos have to move faster to keep up with them. Eventually the whole Twirlywoo Screen is covered in brightly coloured splats, like an abstract painting.

Charlotte thinks that rosemary smells like fresh air but some of her friends are not so keen and don't really like the taste of rosemary on its own. programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: It's bedtime and Maddie is finding out about different things we sleep on and in! At the allotment, Ruby finds a white feather and makes a wish, but she won’t tell Magnus what it is. Magnus keeps trying to guess what Ruby’s wish is. Back at the Big Hub, Moira and Mrs Juniper are busy getting prepared, Moira wants everything to be perfect. Bob, Ruby and Magnus get so carried away with making a home for a caterpillar at the allotment that it’s after one o’clock by the time they realise the time. Oh no, they’ve missed the big announcement! Will Bob win the Green Hero Award? And will Magnus ever find out what Ruby wished for?

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter decides to set Mr Tod and Tommy Brock against each other, he soon finds out that breaking the food chain is harder than it looks.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have made a song. They enjoy playing for others but wish they had a chance to see how they perform together. Duggee explains that they can if they make a music video, which tells a story. There is a lot to prepare beforehand, such as lights, costumes and glitter, and as they prepare, we are immersed into Enid’s dream, where she gives a star performance in her own eclectic music video! The Squirrels are taught to practice their dance moves before filming, to pick the perfect location and to try and put something unexpected into the video. After lots of collaboration, creativity and fun, the Squirrels finally get to watch their own music video and are thrilled at the results.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Popcorn gets sick, Fergie and Kipp offer to help Vida out in the clinic. But their competitive natures get in the way of them working together.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It’s a special day in the veggie aisle because it’s the Dragon Boat Race Festival on Ice. The Supermarket is frozen over and Supertato, Carrot, Broccoli and Tomato practice for the boat race by using chopsticks for oars, but it doesn’t go well as they’re out of sync with each other. Evil Pea arrives with the Cobs, who are rowing in great sync. Evil Pea says they’re going to beat Supertato in the race, and they row away leaving Supertato’s boat behind. Can Supertato help his team to row in harmony?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's the Ducklings' first time playing with a drone, and Weasy is confident he'll beat them in a race. But the Ducklings soon prove him wrong, so Weasy starts cheating to win!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Zog

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the bring-and-buy sale, Rafi insists on keeping her oldest toy, Tommy the T rex. But after a busy day, she realises he’s gone. Worried, she makes a wish to find him, and her wishing wand whisks her and Jake on a wild chase through the park. Finally, back at the bakery, they discover baby Oscar happily playing with Tommy - Amy bought it to cheer him up. Seeing Oscar’s joy, Rafi decides to let him keep Tommy.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran are on a day trip to the sunny seaside with one mission in mind: to build the biggest sandcastle ever built so that Panda can play inside. But JoJo has no luck with building her sandcastle and feels disheartened when she learns about the tide and how it will carry her best sandcastle yet away into the sea! But with Gran Gran on hand, JoJo learns that things don't need to last forever to be special as the pair take lots of pictures for them to keep forever and remember.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny is stuck for ideas for a new tune to make up, so she asks Mother and Major what kind of tune they would most like to hear. Major wants something 'bold and stirring', while Mother would like something 'light and charming'. Tiny's best attempts to please them both come to nothing, until a ride on a Skymoo gives her the inspiration she needs.

programme.title: BeddyByes

Purple Tweety returns to collect Baby Tweety, and MeMo and BaBa feel sleepy on Lullaby Lake. Looking after little ones can be tiring, MeMo and BaBa are ready for BeddyByes!

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Crime drama series based on characters created by Ann Cleeves. DCI Vera Stanhope is on track to uncover an intriguing yet puzzling case when the body of a sickly young girl is found in a railway siding in the middle of nowhere - the girl could be anyone, but the investigation soon turns up twists and turns that makes Vera question who this girl actually was. As a vulnerable young person with a serious health condition, it appears as if her weakened state has allowed someone to take advantage of her and her family's dynamic changed when she wasn't truly part of the family. In a tale of intrigue, betrayal and blurred lines, Vera's investigation questions the meaning of family, care, accountability and eroding trust where care might have come at a cost.

programme.title: Unbelievable Moments Caught On Camera
programme.desc: Astonishing and seemingly-impossible scenes filmed by members of the public and narrated by award-winning actor Roger Allam - the people who recorded these stories and are sharing their memories of these once-in-a-lifetime experiences this time include a kayaker who found himself trapped behind a waterfall in Mexico, a barber who pulled a driver from a burning car in Las Vegas, a family who narrowly escaped a doomed ship in Greece, a student pilot who was forced to land her plane in Michigan without a front wheel, and world champion cyclist Gee Atherton recalling a fall from a mountain in Wales that nearly cost him his life.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: When Christopher's posh old schoolmates arrive for the National Debating Championships final, the Scouse lads fear losing him to his old world. Instead, the groups begin to bond until a drunken factory break-in, crashed forklift and night in the cells forces Christopher to confront where he belongs. In the debate final, Christopher delivers a personal argument about why people divide themselves and how belonging to two worlds can be a strength. Meanwhile, Anna's return fractures Aimee and Wayne's alliance when she offers a different version of the past, leaving Aimee torn between loyalty to her dad and the mum she never stopped missing. Lewis's redemption arc implodes when his public apology tour exposes more chaos than growth, forcing Kieron to stage an intervention.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: When Christopher's posh old schoolmates arrive for the National Debating Championships final, the Scouse lads fear losing him to his old world. Instead, the groups begin to bond until a drunken factory break-in, crashed forklift and night in the cells forces Christopher to confront where he belongs. In the debate final, Christopher delivers a personal argument about why people divide themselves and how belonging to two worlds can be a strength. Meanwhile, Anna's return fractures Aimee and Wayne's alliance when she offers a different version of the past, leaving Aimee torn between loyalty to her dad and the mum she never stopped missing. Lewis's redemption arc implodes when his public apology tour exposes more chaos than growth, forcing Kieron to stage an intervention.

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Crime drama series based on characters created by Ann Cleeves. DCI Vera Stanhope is on track to uncover an intriguing yet puzzling case when the body of a sickly young girl is found in a railway siding in the middle of nowhere - the girl could be anyone, but the investigation soon turns up twists and turns that makes Vera question who this girl actually was. As a vulnerable young person with a serious health condition, it appears as if her weakened state has allowed someone to take advantage of her and her family's dynamic changed when she wasn't truly part of the family. In a tale of intrigue, betrayal and blurred lines, Vera's investigation questions the meaning of family, care, accountability and eroding trust where care might have come at a cost.

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Crime drama series based on characters created by Ann Cleeves. DCI Vera Stanhope is on track to uncover an intriguing yet puzzling case when the body of a sickly young girl is found in a railway siding in the middle of nowhere - the girl could be anyone, but the investigation soon turns up twists and turns that makes Vera question who this girl actually was. As a vulnerable young person with a serious health condition, it appears as if her weakened state has allowed someone to take advantage of her and her family's dynamic changed when she wasn't truly part of the family. In a tale of intrigue, betrayal and blurred lines, Vera's investigation questions the meaning of family, care, accountability and eroding trust where care might have come at a cost.

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Crime drama series based on characters created by Ann Cleeves. DCI Vera Stanhope is on track to uncover an intriguing yet puzzling case when the body of a sickly young girl is found in a railway siding in the middle of nowhere - the girl could be anyone, but the investigation soon turns up twists and turns that makes Vera question who this girl actually was. As a vulnerable young person with a serious health condition, it appears as if her weakened state has allowed someone to take advantage of her and her family's dynamic changed when she wasn't truly part of the family. In a tale of intrigue, betrayal and blurred lines, Vera's investigation questions the meaning of family, care, accountability and eroding trust where care might have come at a cost.

Instead, the groups begin to bond until a drunken factory break-in, crashed forklift and night in the cells forces Christopher to confront where he belongs. In the debate final, Christopher delivers a personal argument about why people divide themselves and how belonging to two worlds can be a strength. Meanwhile, Anna's return fractures Aimee and Wayne's alliance when she offers a different version of the past, leaving Aimee torn between loyalty to her dad and the mum she never stopped missing. Lewis's redemption arc implodes when his public apology tour exposes more chaos than growth, forcing Kieron to stage an intervention.

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Crime drama series based on characters created by Ann Cleeves. DCI Vera Stanhope is on track to uncover an intriguing yet puzzling case when the body of a sickly young girl is found in a railway siding in the middle of nowhere - the girl could be anyone, but the investigation soon turns up twists and turns that makes Vera question who this girl actually was. As a vulnerable young person with a serious health condition, it appears as if her weakened state has allowed someone to take advantage of her and her family's dynamic changed when she wasn't truly part of the family. In a tale of intrigue, betrayal and blurred lines, Vera's investigation questions the meaning of family, care, accountability and eroding trust where care might have come at a cost.

programme.desc: When Christopher's posh old schoolmates arrive for the National Debating Championships final, the Scouse lads fear losing him to his old world. Meanwhile, Anna's return fractures Aimee and Wayne's alliance when she offers a different version of the past, leaving Aimee torn between loyalty to her dad and the mum she never stopped missing. Lewis's redemption arc implodes when his public apology tour exposes more chaos than growth, forcing Kieron to stage an intervention.
